title: Open-square exchange from restriction of direct image
statement:
Use the finite coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}$. Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U'&\xrightarrow{g_U}&U\\
{\scriptstyle j'}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle j}\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$

be a Cartesian square with $j,j'$
open immersions.
On the small pro-etale sites,
the extension-by-zero functors
and derived pullbacks
admit a canonical natural isomorphism

$$
b_g:Lg^*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!Lg_U^*.
$$

Its restriction to $U'$ is the identity, after the pullback
identifications. These isomorphisms respect identity squares and
pasting of Cartesian squares.
(Source for the etale version:
[Stacks, Tag 03S6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03S6),
Lemma 59.70.5, the underived statement $j'_!f'^{-1}=f^{-1}j_!$ on
sheaves; the derived form and the compatibilities are proved below.)

proof.text: Use the existing canonical fixed-coefficient pro-etale open base-change map. It is invertible for a Cartesian square because it is the conjugate of weakly etale base change. The existing mate calculation identifies its mate under the two open adjunctions with the canonical pullback-square isomorphism. Transport all four functors and the map through the fixed intrinsic coefficient realization equivalences. Expanding the transported units and counits, using their naturality and the equivalence triangle identities, identifies this transported map with sfIntrinsicOpenMate. Thus this specified ordinary mate, rather than an arbitrarily selected comparison, is invertible.

source.place: Open-square exchange: canonical mate, restriction normalization, identity and pasting; exact termwise descent

proof.text: The fixed-coefficient pullback compositors satisfy their identity and pasting equations. Transport these equations by the same realization equivalences, inserting the intermediate equivalence unit in every compositor. Naturality and the unit-inverse cancellation show that the intrinsic pullback squares satisfy both pasting equations and the identity equations with precisely the published intrinsic pullback compositors and identity maps. No change of scalar action or unnormalized pullback comparison is made.

source.place: Open-square exchange: canonical mate, restriction normalization, identity and pasting; exact termwise descent

proof.text: Apply injectivity of the mate equivalence to the ordinary horizontal and vertical exchange equations. The generic mate pasting identities turn them into the pullback-square equations of the previous step. For vertical pasting, the open-extension compositor is the unique adjoint comparison preserving the composite units, so its conjugate is the inverse pullback compositor. The corresponding identity comparison has the inverse pullback identity as its conjugate. The identity mate identities therefore also give both ordinary identity laws.

source.place: Open-square exchange: canonical mate, restriction normalization, identity and pasting; exact termwise descent

proof.text: Fully faithful fixed-coefficient open extension remains fully faithful after transport, so both ordinary open units are invertible. The generic unit equation for the mate identifies pullback of the source unit followed by the pullback square with the target unit followed by pullback of the ordinary reverse exchange. This proves the required normalization after cancelling the inverse exchange.

source.place: Open-square exchange: canonical mate, restriction normalization, identity and pasting; exact termwise descent

proof.text: All intrinsic functors are additive and exact. Descend the ordinary maps termwise to the unbounded derived categories. The resulting square comparison is the inverse exact-functor compositor, followed by the localized ordinary comparison, followed by the forward compositor, exactly as in sfIntrinsicDerivedOpenMate. Localization natural-transformation extensionality, checked on the homotopy-category quotient, carries the unit equation to the derived unit equation. Exact derived square composition and identity comparison carry both pasting and identity laws to the published derived compositors.

source.place: Open-square exchange: canonical mate, restriction normalization, identity and pasting; exact termwise descent

proof.text: Define the exchange as the inverse of the specified derived mate, and invert the proved mate identity and pasting equations. Cancellation with the derived mate gives the restriction equation. Assemble these maps and equations into SfOpenSquareExchangeData and specialize to the finite coefficient quotient A_{E,n}. The already proved unique, section-unit-normalized pullback-model identification transports the intrinsic pullbacks to the published constant-ring pullbacks used by constantOpenSquareExchange. This final conjugation preserves the specified exchange and its equations.

blueprint_update.statement:
Use the finite coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}$. Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U'&\xrightarrow{g_U}&U\\
{\scriptstyle j'}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle j}\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y
\end{array}
$$

be a Cartesian square with $j,j'$
open immersions.
On the small pro-etale sites,
the extension-by-zero functors
and derived pullbacks
admit a canonical natural isomorphism

$$
b_g:Lg^*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!Lg_U^*.
$$

Its restriction to $U'$ is the identity, after the pullback
identifications. These isomorphisms respect identity squares and
pasting of Cartesian squares.

proof.text:
Restriction along an open immersion is localization of the site:
an object $V\to U$ is also an object over $Y$.
For a sheaf $Q$ on $Y'$, the direct-image formula gives

$$
(j^*g_*Q)(V)=Q(V\times_Y Y')
=(g_{U*}j'^*Q)(V).
$$

The equality respects restrictions and coverings on the site of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Thus $j^*g_*=g_{U*}j'^*$,
with all comparison maps specified on sections.

The exact functor $j'^*$ preserves injectives and K-injectives:
its left adjoint $j'_!$ is exact by
[def-weil-extension-by-zero]. For K-injectives this follows
directly by applying the adjunction to Hom complexes against an
acyclic complex. Thus a K-injective resolution of $Q$ computes
both sides of

$$
j^*Rg_*Q\simeq Rg_{U*}j'^*Q,
$$

using [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Taking left adjoints,
with the exact inverse-image pullbacks of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], gives
$Lg^*j_!\simeq j'_!Lg_U^*$. This defines $b_g$.
On $U'$ the section equality is the identity, so its mate has the
stated normalization. The section equalities for two pasted squares
compose to the equality for the outer square. The uniqueness of
left adjoints with their adjunction data proves the pasting and
identity assertions. This proof uses no claim that ordinary
geometric stalks detect arbitrary pro-etale sheaves.
